SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGS
Translation of a statement made by the five delegates of
the Southwest clique on their arrival in Shanghai on July 9,
No. D. 7456
1936

We five persons are going to attend the Second Plenary
Session to be held in Nanking as representatives of the
Southwest clique. We left Canton on the 6th and arrived
in Hongkong on the 7th, and travelled on the s.s. "President
Jefferson" to Shanghai. Many people are anxious to ascertain
the latest political developments in the Southwest. Conse-
quently, we will give you a true account of the circumstances
surrounding the policy of the Southwest Authorities in
deciding to resist the Japanese in order to save the nation.

Since September 18, 1931, the whole nation has been
inclined to the policy of resistance, especially the people at
the Southwest. However, the people have continued to bear
their sufferings patiently until the present time when the
critical situation in North China has convinced the people
that the nation has reached its final stage of existence and
that should no efforts be made to offer resistance, the
nation will collapse. Kwangtung is the birthplace of the
revolution, and the people of Kwangtung have already assumed
more than their share of responsibility in aiding the nation.
In view of the external aggression, the Kwangtung Authorities
felt that it was impossible to see the nation and country
destroyed without raising a hand. Accordingly, they decided to
start the national salvation movement by reorganizing the troops
of Kwangtung and Kwangsi and renaming them the Anti-Japanese
National Salvation Army. They have made all preparations for
an expedition, and meanwhile requested the Central Government
by telegram to take the leadership and organize national
resistance. The aim of the movements is to express determination
by realities instead of empty speeches. Unfortunately owing
to rumours the Central Government entertained suspicion of
the Southwest and declared their actions to be imprudent. This

特别支部规章
西南派系五名代表于7月9日抵达上海时所发表声明的译文
编号 D. 7456
1936年

我们五人作为西南派系的代表，将前往南京参加即将举行的第二届全体会议。我们于6日离开广州，7日抵达香港，随后乘坐“杰斐逊总统”号轮船（s.s. "President Jefferson"）前往上海。许多人急于了解西南地区的最新政治动态。因此，我们将向各位如实陈述西南当局决定抗日救国政策的相关背景情况。

自1931年9月18日以来，全国上下均倾向于抵抗政策，西南地区民众尤甚。然而，民众一直忍辱负重至今，直到华北局势危急，使民众确信国家已存亡绝续之秋，若不努力抵抗，国家必将崩溃。广东是革命的发源地，广东人民在援助国家方面已经承担了超出其份额的责任。鉴于外敌侵略，广东当局认为不能坐视国家灭亡而不采取行动。因此，他们决定通过重组广东和广西的部队，并将其更名为“抗日救国军”，来启动救国运动。他们已为出征做好了一切准备，同时致电中央政府，请求其发挥领导作用，组织全国抵抗。此次运动的目的是以实际行动而非空谈来表达决心。不幸的是，由于谣言，中央政府对西南地区产生怀疑，并宣称其行动轻率。此

misunderstanding is to be regretted. The Southwestern
military authorities, following the receipt of telegraphic
instructions from the Central Government, at once withdrew
the small number of troops who were sent out first and were
waiting for further instructions, to their billets. It is
hoped that at the forthcoming 2nd plenary session, a plan
will be devised to save the nation by resisting Japan.
Apart from submitting the case for the Southwest to the
Session, we hope that the Session will accept the five
requests contained in the proposal and take the leadership
in resisting Japan so that the nation will be saved and the
wishes of the people throughout the country will be granted.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. B. REGIST:
S. B. D. 7456
J.1, Special Branch. Staff. 30
Date July 9, 1936.

REPORT

Subject Allegation regarding Arrival in Shanghai of representatives
from the South West.

Made by D.I. Fan Lien-pih Forwarded by. [Signature]

With reference to the report that representatives
from the South West were to arrive in Shanghai en route to
Nanking to make appeals to the Central Government, inquiries
have been made and it has been ascertained that the following
vessels have arrived in Shanghai from South China since
July 7 :-

s.s. "Franken"
s.s. "Fushimi Maru"
s.s. "Nellore"
s.s. "Preussen"
s.s. "Boikow"
s.s. "Ajax."
s.s. "An-shing"
s.s. "President Jefferson"

There were no large or small groups of passengers on board these
boats whose movements gave rise to suspicion.

Eight official delegates of the South West authorities
to the 2nd Plenary Session of the C.E.C. of the Kuomintang to
be held in Nanking on July 10 travelled in the s.s. "President
Jefferson", which arrived here at 8.30 a.m. July 9 and berthed
at Buoys No.12 and 13. There names are given below :-

Hwang Ling-su (黃麟書), Wong Zien-sung (王泉笙),
Teng Ching-yang (鄧青陽), Li Ning-jen (李任仁),
Li Chi-an (李綺庵), Tsai Kwang-siu (崔廣秀),
Li Foh-ling (李福林) and Li Ts-wan (李次溫).

They are residing in the Park Hotel, Bubbling Well Road.

Seven members of the staff of the Aviation Bureau
in the South West, who are believed to have surrendered to
the Nanking Government, arrived in the same vessel. They

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, July 9, 1936

Delegates
Of Canton
Land Here

Important Kuomintang
Session In Nanking
Opens Tomorrow

Cantonese Dodge
Local Newsmen

Demand For Immediate
War Against Japan
Anticipated

With the five Southwest delegates in Shanghai and more than 150 members already in Nanking, the momentous Second Plenary Session of the Central Executive and Supervisory Committees of the Kuomintang will be formally opened in the capital city early tomorrow morning.

Never in the history of the Kuomintang has an agenda of such importance been placed before the C.E.C. and C.S.C. sessions. The Kuomintang leaders attending this meeting will be formally asked to discuss a resolution demanding a declaration of war with Japan, which is to be submitted by the Southwestern delegates who arrived from Canton via Hongkong on the Dollar liner President Jefferson this morning.

Starts Tomorrow

While it is generally believed that the resolution will not be given much deliberation at the session, other resolutions aimed at the prevention of the Southwest's purported anti-Japanese drive and at the unification of the nation will be fully discussed in a concerted effort to avoid internal dissension, political or military.

The first item on the program for the opening of the momentous C.E.C. and C.S.C. session is scheduled to take place at 6 o'clock tomorrow morning at the mausoleum of the founder of the party, the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen. Members attending the session will pay their respects to the leader and hold the opening ceremony there. A preliminary session will follow at 8 o'clock at the Central Kuomintang Headquarters at which the formalities of selection of a presidium and creation of various sub-committees will be completed.

Big Budget

A budget of $81,000 has been approved by the national government to cover the expenses of the meeting. Elaborate precautions are taken by authorities in Nanking to prevent disturbances during the session. Heavy detachments of police and gendarmes have been posted in and out the Central Tangpu building. Still vividly mindful of the attempt on the life of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, then president of the Executive Yuan, on November 1, last year, the guard will bar all newsmen and persons not directly connected with the conference from the building.

The five Southwest delegates were literally "smuggled" into Shanghai this morning. When they reached port on the President Jefferson and before the handful of early-rising newspapermen could find time to board the Dollar liner from the tender, the delegates were escorted by an official from the City Government of Greater Shanghai into a waiting launch belonging to the Public Safety Bureau. Despite the protest of Customs officers, the launch carried the passengers away.

War Demanded

Approached later, the delegates, Messrs. Huang Ling-shu, Li Chi-an, Li Jen-jen, Tsui Kwang-shu and Teng Tsiang-yang, issued a written statement in which they vouched for the sincerity of the Southwest's "anti-Japanese expedition" and confirmed reports that the Southwest Political Council is submitting a five-point resolution to the C.E.C. session demanding immediate severance of relations with Japan, abrogation of all "humiliating" Sino-Japanese agreements, the use of armed force to prevent an increase of the Japanese garrison in North China, restoration of freedom of speech and liberty of the people, and that the Central Government take the initiative and lead the country to war.

The Southwest delegates are proceeding to Nanking by train tonight. Leaving for the capital city tonight also are Messrs. T. V. Soong, Wu Te-chen, Pan Kung-chan, Yang Cho-kan, Hsieh Chieh and other C. E. C. members. A large party of them left for Nanking last night. It is expected that approximately 190 out of the 255 regular and reserve C. E. C. and C. S. C. members in all parts of China will attend the session.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年7月9日，星期四

广州代表
抵沪

国民党重要会议
明日在南京开幕

粤方代表躲避
本地记者

预计将要求
立即对日开战

随着五名西南代表抵达上海，以及已有150多名成员到达南京，国民党中央执行委员会和中央监察委员会具有重大意义的第二届全体会议将于明晨在首都正式开幕。

在国民党历史上，从未有如此重要的议程提交给中执委和中监会会议。出席此次会议的国民党领导人将被正式要求讨论一项对日宣战的决议，该决议将由今晨乘坐美元航线“杰斐逊总统”号轮船从广州经香港抵达的西南代表提交。

明日开始

虽然人们普遍认为该决议在会议上不会得到太多审议，但其他旨在防止西南所谓抗日行动以及实现国家统一的决议将在协调努力下得到充分讨论，以避免内部的政治或军事分歧。

隆重的中执委和中监会会议开幕议程的第一项定于明晨6点在党父、已故孙中山博士的陵墓举行。与会成员将向领袖致敬并在那里举行开幕式。随后将于8点在国民党中央总部举行预备会议，完成主席团选举及各小组委员会成立的程序。

巨额预算

国民政府已批准81,000美元的预算以支付会议费用。南京当局采取了严密的预防措施，以防止会议期间发生骚乱。大量警察和宪兵部署在中央党部大楼内外。当局仍清晰记得去年11月1日时任行政院院长汪精卫先生遇刺未遂事件，警卫将禁止所有记者和与会议无直接关系的人员进入大楼。

这五名西南代表今晨实际上是“偷运”进上海的。当他们乘坐“杰斐逊总统”号抵达港口时，在少数早起的记者来得及从接驳船登上美元航线轮船之前，代表们在大上海市政府一名官员的护送下，进入了一艘等候着的公安局汽艇。尽管海关人员提出抗议，汽艇还是载着乘客离去。

要求开战

随后，代表们黄麟书、李绮庵、李任仁、崔广秀和邓青阳先生发表了一份书面声明，保证西南“抗日出征”的诚意，并证实了西南政务委员会正在向中执委会议提交一份五点决议的消息，要求立即断绝与日本的关系，废除所有“屈辱”的中日协定，使用武力阻止日军在华北增兵，恢复言论自由和人民 liberty，并由中央政府采取主动，领导国家进行战争。

西南代表将于今晚乘火车前往南京。宋子文（T. V. Soong）、吴铁城（Wu Te-chen）、潘公展（Pan Kung-chan）、杨卓干（Yang Cho-kan）、谢介（Hsieh Chieh）及其他中执委成员也将于今晚前往首都。他们中的大批人员已于昨晚出发。预计在全国各地的255名正式和候补中执委及中监会成员中，约有190人将出席会议。
